newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's TPS sees 250,000 subscribers by end 1997.
newsitem.headline: France's TPS sees 250,000 subscribers by end 1997.

text.p: Television Par Satellite (TPS) aims to have over 250,000 subscribers by the end of this year, and to have signed up 150,000 of these by the end of June, managing director Cyrille Peloux said on Thursday.
"We hope to have 150,000 subscribers by the end of June and over 250,000 by the end of 1997," he told a news conference.
Peloux also said that 25,000 of the 80,000 subscribers who have signed up with TPS so far have now received their decoder.
He said the delay in delivering decoders, which has dogged TPS since it was launched last December, should be over by May.

TPS, one of two French digital satellite television offerings, is controlled by terrestrial TV channel M6-Metropole TV and its parents, Lyonnaise des Eaux and Luxembourg's CLT, itself part of Audiofina.
Terrestrial channel TF1 also has a 25 percent stake in TPS, and public channels France 2 and France 3 together with France Telecom hold the remaining 25 percent.
